title: Input hardening follow-ups: debounce for legacy ButtonState consumers + HID adapter deadzone (from TASK-023 review)
description: Two deferred items surfaced by TASK-023 (InputInterpreter, GDD T-101). (1) Legacy un-debounced edges: upstream ButtonState.Pressed bakes edge detection in the Unity-side adapter with no debounce guarantee; the new InputInterpreter re-derives debounced edges for itself, but existing consumers of raw ButtonState.Pressed (e.g. AporreaMicrogame) still receive un-debounced signals. Decide: migrate legacy microgames to InputInterpreter-derived edges (preferred, per GDD 3.2 architecture where the interpreter owns edge detection) or add debounce upstream. (2) Deadzone at the trust boundary: InputInterpreter.ToDirection8 uses raw sign with no deadzone (consistent with existing InputSnapshot.CardinalDirection, correct for digital sticks); the Framework HID->InputSnapshot adapter (GDD Annex D.1 row 'Adaptador HID -> InputSnapshot', to be verified against 3.2 in a later ticket) MUST apply a deadzone (e.g. WithDeadZone) before snapshots reach Core, or analog noise of +/-0.0001 mints full directions. Fold item (2) into the adapter verification ticket when it is created; this ticket then covers only item (1). Origin: TASK-023 reviewer findings LOW-2 + developer-flagged delta (review 2026-07-07, APPROVE-WITH-NITS).
acceptance_criteria: Every microgame that consumes button edges gets them debounced: either via migration to InputInterpreter signals or via upstream debounce in the adapter — decision recorded in ticket comments with rationale
The HID->InputSnapshot adapter applies a deadzone before Core sees stick values (verified by test or recorded as handled in the adapter ticket)
Fast suite and Unity EditMode suite stay green

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
DECISION RECORD (AC1) — Phase A inventory by dev-t101 (full report in session log, 2026-07-07 ~14:2xZ), independently verified by orchestrator grep (ButtonState.Pressed, repo-wide: production consumers exactly = AporreaMicrogame, TimingMicrogame, ApuntaMicrogame-v1, SampleTapMicrogame; InputInterpreter is the debounce OWNER not a raw consumer; ArcadeInputBridge is the PRODUCER; Esquiva/Recolecta never read ButtonState). Ratified dispositions:

(1) AporreaMicrogame (raw per-tick edge counting, highest exposure), TimingMicrogame + ApuntaMicrogame-v1 (one-shot latch on first edge, narrower exposure): DEFER to TASK-034 (GDD T-107). Rationale: the MicrogameDefinitionMigrator class doc (TASK-030) already designates T-107 as the reconciliation point for the four pre-GDD legacy ids (aporrea/apunta/timing/recolecta) against the canonical MECH_01..09 set; migrating them to owned InputInterpreter instances NOW would introduce a real behavior change (the 2-tick debounce-confirm detection delay would shift pinned test expectations) and is very likely thrown away wholesale when T-107 rewrites or retires them v2-native (the pattern Reacciona/Apunta-v2 already use). The un-debounced edge is a LOW-severity nit (origin: TASK-023 review APPROVE-WITH-NITS LOW-2), not an active bug; Timing/Apunta's latch already absorbs the main bounce failure mode. Carry-in comment added to TASK-034.

(2) SampleTapMicrogame: NO ACTION — not a GDD mechanic; deterministic lifecycle-test scaffold consumed only by MicrogameLifecycleTests; zero player-facing exposure.

(3) Deadzone at the HID trust boundary (AC2): RECORDED AS HANDLED IN THE ADAPTER TICKET — TASK-054 filed with the named item (InputSnapshot.WithDeadZone at ArcadeInputBridge.UpdateSlot, ~0.15-0.2 starting threshold as a calibration call) plus the full GDD Annex D.1 'Adaptador HID → InputSnapshot' row verification the TASK-023 review originally scoped; verification via ArcadeInputBridgeTests PlayMode + Unity gate. Confirmed present-state evidence: UpdateSlot passes raw stick.x/y into InputSnapshot with no deadzone.

AC3: satisfied by no-change — zero code touched under this ticket (fast suite untouched at 554/554; EditMode leg trivially unaffected). This ticket closes decision-only: no diff exists, so no code reviewer was spawned; the verification applied was the orchestrator's independent inventory grep + the ratification record above.
